evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.52 mg/L at t=48.0 to 4.40 mg/L at t=48.2 and declines monotonically to 3.27 mg/L at t=52.0 (decision time)
Linear fit of receiving DO2 over t=48.2-52.0 gives slope -0.257 mg/L/h, projecting ~2.5 mg/L by t=56 and breach of the 2.0 mg/L minimum by t~58 under KEEP
Receiving P assay: 0.0 g/L at t=24, 1.15 g/L at t=36, 3.27 g/L at t=48 - active productive metabolism driving oxygen demand
Source batches (source-1/2/3) never show DO2 below ~7.4 mg/L after their benign t=24-28 dip; receiving's persistent low-DO excursion is anomalous
allowed_actions: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15] (feed unchanged); reduce_feed options sacrifice 20-40% feed-driven production
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows an anomalous sustained decline (11.5 -> 4.4 mg/L abrupt drop at t=48.2, then ~-0.26 mg/L/h) toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum, with projected breach by ~t=58 under KEEP. Active product accumulation (3.27 g/L at t=48) confirms real oxygen demand. increase_air (1.15x) adds oxygen-transfer capacity without any feed cut, retaining full product mass — the least-destructive intervention that addresses the oxygen constraint. Feed reduction is held as escalation if DO does not stabilize.
submission.uncertainty: Air scale factors and OUR/OTR parameters are hidden; the 1.15x increase may be insufficient to reverse the decline if demand keeps growing (DO headroom at decision time is only ~1.3 mg/L). If DO continues falling below ~3 mg/L after intervention, escalation to combined (0.8x feed + 1.15x air) would be justified. The delayed product assays (4 h turnaround) also mean current true P/DO state estimates carry lag uncertainty.

evidence: Receiving DO2 observations: 11.52 mg/L at t=48.0h collapsing to 4.40 mg/L at t=48.2h, declining to 3.27 mg/L at t=52.0h
Receiving delayed assay P: 3.27 g/L at t=48h (sample), comparable to source batches (3.0-3.1 g/L) prior to the transfer loss
Source batches (source-1/2/3) show no such DO2 collapse after 48h, indicating a receiving-specific transfer failure; physical_forward_model estimates transfer multiplier ~0.49 after change at t=48h

Forward-model comparison at t=52h: keep min DO 1.40 mg/L / 4.4h below limit / 174.8 kg; combined 1.48 mg/L / 4.4h / 181.1 kg; strong_feed_reduction 1.66 mg/L / 2.8h / 203.5 kg (best of bounded options)
strong_feed_reduction retains product mass and avoids stop (stop counts zero production)
submission.rationale: A receiving-specific oxygen-transfer failure began at t=48 h: DO2 fell from ~11.5 to ~4.4 mg/L within 0.2 h and continued declining to 3.27 mg/L at t=52 h, on track to breach the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Source batches show no analogous collapse, confirming a receiving-process anomaly rather than normal trajectory. Among bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed, 1.15 air) best preserves feasibility: it cuts oxygen demand most, giving the highest projected minimum DO (~1.66 mg/L), the shortest interval below the oxygen limit (~2.8 h), the smallest oxygen deficit, and the highest retained product mass (~203 kg vs ~175 kg under keep). A stop would forfeit all counted production, and milder options leave longer/ deeper oxygen-limit violations. Recommendation is advisory only; no equipment action is executed.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; all options it evaluated remain nominally infeasible over the horizon, though strong_feed_reduction is the best-bounded and has feasible members in the sensitivity ensemble (min DO range 1.14-2.65 mg/L). The true receiving-process parameters (transfer loss magnitude, biomass state) are hidden, so the projected minimum DO could be better or worse than modeled; continued DO2 monitoring is needed and a stop contingency should be reviewed if DO2 falls near 2.0 mg/L despite intervention.
